items.title: The finite Potts Gibbs matrix is well-defined at every finite inverse temperature
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: For $Q\in\{2,3,4\}$, $L\geq1$, real coefficients $J_i$, and finite real $\beta$, the matrix $H_{Q,L}(\mathbf J)$ defined on the Potts-clock chain is self-adjoint. With the spectral definitions $B_\beta$, $Z_\beta$, and $\rho_\beta$ from that definition, $Z_\beta>0$ and $\rho_\beta$ is a positive semidefinite matrix of trace one. This is a finite-dimensional mathematical fact; it makes no thermodynamic-limit or empirical claim.

references.title: D. Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §7.4 Variational Density Matrix Method
references.locator: §7.4, The variational principle, lines 1352–1379: positive finite-level Boltzmann weights and the normalized partition function; the local spectral proof handles the noncommuting finite matrix.

items.title: Spin-half exchange realizes Temperley-Lieb at loop two
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: Let $N\geq1$ and let $\mathcal H_N=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N}$ have the standard tensor-product Hermitian inner product, linear in its first argument, with $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$ orthonormal on each factor. For $1\leq i<N$, let $s_i$ be the swap of tensor factors $i,i+1$, let $|\omega\rangle=(|01\rangle-|10\rangle)/\sqrt2$, and let $P_i=I^{\otimes(i-1)}\otimes|\omega\rangle\langle\omega|\otimes I^{\otimes(N-i-1)}$ be the projection onto this singlet on those two factors. Put $e_i:=I-s_i$. Then these are the loop-weight-two Temperley-Lieb generators. In the Hecke normalization $g_i(q):=qI-e_i$, at $q=1$ one has $g_i(1)=s_i$. items.title: Local spectrum and noncommuting terms
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: Fix $Q\in\{2,3,4\}$ and the two-site open chain $L=2$. Let $\kappa,\lambda\in\mathbb R$ with $\kappa\neq0$ and finite $\beta\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, and set $H=-\kappa e_1-\lambda e_2=-\sqrt Q(\kappa P_1+\lambda D_{12})$. A classical diagonal replacement here means a density matrix diagonal in the computational basis $|ab\rangle$. The exact finite Gibbs density $\rho_\beta$ of this matrix is not diagonal in that basis. Moreover $P_1,D_{12}$ are nontrivial projections with spectrum $\{0,1\}$, satisfy $P_1D_{12}P_1=Q^{-1}P_1$, and do not commute.
